title: 1 Knight VS 3 Pawns
reviewNotes: Three branches, 13 exact positions from the complete seven-piece Black-to-move root. ...Nb7 axb6+ ...Kb8 a4 ...Ka8 a5 ...Nc5# is actual Black mate, with both pawn pushes forced. ...bxa5 Kxa5 and ...Nc4 axb6+ ...Nxb6 are exact draws. The practice objective and orientation follow Black; expected outcomes remain White-relative.
transcript: Sometimes one brave warrior can be enough to push back an entire army. In this position, black is left with only one knight and one pawn against the three white pawns that are trying [music] to promote on this corner of the board. And it seems like black has no way to prevent the white king to trade off one of his pawns to secure a draw, if not a win. For example, if black takes this pawn, white is going to capture back and now the knight is not going to be enough to win this game in any way. And if black tries any funny tricks like knight to c4 trying to attack this pawn. Well, now white is going to trade like this with check, we can win back the pawn. But again, there's no way to make any progress. So the black king might consider offering a peaceful draw to the white king. But that would be a massive mistake because black can indeed win this position. And the secret to winning this endame is to realize that these white pawns are going to play against their own king. The first very precise move that black needs to play is knight to B7. White [music] has to take this pawn. If you play a king move, which is the only other option, black is simply going to win this pawn. And now you're preventing the trade of the pawn. And after white pushes, the knight is going to come back. Now you only have two options. Either this move or this move. And both of them fail to knight to C5 with either a forb picking up this pawn or with an attack on the pawn. You cannot push because I'm going to take like this. And if you don't push and you come back with the king, I'm going to win the pawn anyway. But of course, after knight B7, the king can simply take this pawn. And some of you might think, well, this doesn't make any sense. How is this knight alone going to be able to checkmate the white king against three pawns? Well, black has found an incredible sequence. And he follows up with king to B8. Now trapping the white king inside a wall mainly created by his own soldiers. The white king is actually in Zukswag. The best thing would be for white to not move anything and simply pass the move. And there would be no way for black to win this game. But the gods of chess do not allow such cowardice. And so the white king has to push the white pawn. But now the black king is going to go to a8 placing the white king in zukwang once again. The only move that white can play is a5. And now we have created a prison with the white pawns. This king was betrayed by his own allies.
